Complete the lab page's package check in the Console first. Keep the supplied
library calls so the report works in a fresh R session. Do not put
`install.packages()` in this report. Replace **Your name** with your name.

The data-creation code is supplied and uses synthetic data.
Follow tasks 1–8 on the lab page. Brief comments in each chunk remind you of
useful syntax; write your code and explanations under the relevant heading.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(lubridate)

# Synthetic teaching data, not real patients.
patient_lookup <- data.frame(
  id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04"),
  arm = c("control", "treated", "treated", "control")
)
marker_wide <- data.frame(
  id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P05"),
  marker_w0 = c(4.1, 5.2, 6.0, 4.8),
  marker_w4 = c(4.4, 4.7, 5.1, 4.9)
)
raw_patients <- data.frame(
  id = c(" p01 ", "p02", " P03", "p04 "),
  arm = c(" Control ", "TREATED", " treated ", "control"),
  enrolled = c("2026-09-01", "2026-09-03", "2026-10-01", "2026-10-02"),
  note = c(" first   visit ", " repeat sample", "repeat  visit ", "first visit")
)
```

## 1. Row units and keys

State the row unit in each table and identify the IDs present in only one table.

```{r task-1}
# Check both tables with count(id) |> filter(n > 1).
# Print the tables to inspect their IDs.
```

## 2. Join and inspect unmatched participants

Predict which participants each join will retain, then check your prediction.

```{r task-2}
# Starting syntax: left_join(marker_wide, patient_lookup, by = "id").
# Save as joined_wide; compare nrow() and inspect missing arm values.
# Use anti_join() in both directions; compare inner_join() with left_join().
# Reverse the left join and save as enrollment_report.
```

Explain who lacks treatment information and who lacks measurements in the
enrollment report.

## 3. Wide to long

Predict the number of rows and state the new row unit.

```{r task-3}
# Save marker_long using pivot_longer() on marker_wide.
# cols = starts_with("marker_w"), names_to = "week",
# names_prefix = "marker_w", values_to = "marker".
# Then mutate(week = as.integer(week)); check nrow() and one participant.
```

Name an analysis or display that benefits from the long format.

## 4. Return to wide

```{r task-4}
# Save marker_back using pivot_wider() on marker_long.
# id_cols = id, names_from = week, values_from = marker,
# names_prefix = "marker_w".
# Sort marker_back and marker_wide with arrange(id) before comparing them.
```

Compare IDs, column names, and values. Why is wide form useful for calculating
week-4 minus baseline?

## 5. Clean and search text

```{r task-5}
# Create patients_text from raw_patients with mutate().
# ID example: str_to_upper(str_trim(id)).
# For arm and note, combine str_squish() with str_to_lower().
# Filter with str_detect(note, fixed("repeat")); select id and note.
```

Keep `raw_patients` unchanged. Explain the difference between `str_trim()`
and `str_squish()`.

## 6. Factor labels and order

```{r task-6}
# Save patients_factor from patients_text.
# In mutate(), use fct_recode(): NEW label = "old label".
# Map control to Control and treated to Treatment.
# Use fct_relevel(arm, "Control"); inspect levels() and count(arm).
```

Which step changes labels and which changes only their order?

## 7. Parse dates

```{r task-7}
# Save patients_clean from patients_factor with mutate().
# Create enrolled_date = ymd(enrolled).
# Add enrolled_year and enrolled_month with year() and month().
# Compare source/parsed dates; filter(is.na(enrolled_date)) finds failures.
```

Explain why `"03/04/2026"` needs a documented input convention. Compare
`mdy()` and `dmy()` on that string.

### 5. Optional join detail: relationship check

This is the only chunk that permits an intentional error.

```{r practice-5, error=TRUE}
conflicting_lookup <- data.frame(
  id = c("P01", "P01", "P02", "P03", "P04"),
  arm = c("control", "treated", "treated", "treated", "control")
)
# Join marker_long to conflicting_lookup by id; inspect count(id) and nrow().
# Repeat with relationship = "many-to-one" to display the expected error.
```

Explain why rows multiply and why keeping the first treatment record is not
automatically a valid correction.

### 6. Optional window example: previous visit

```{r practice-6}
# Start with marker_long: arrange(id, week), then group_by(id).
# In mutate(), calculate change = marker - lag(marker), then ungroup().
```

Explain why each participant's first change is missing.
